newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Feb 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Feb 19.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Senate on Tuesday adopted a resolution reaffirming its irrevocable opposition to any move to amend the Constitution. (MANILA BULLETIN/INQUIRER/STAR)

- The Cabinet committee formed by President Ramos to investigate an alleged anomalous land deal between the Public Estates Authority and the Amari Coastal Bay Development Corp said it found no evidence to back charges of bribery in the deal. (STAR)
- President Ramos said on Tuesday six years in power is enough for him as he dismissed allegations he would engineer a military coup to install himself as a dictator. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- The government has raised the possibility of a "less than graceful" exit from 30 years of International Monetary Fund tutelage should Congress fail to pass the comprehensive tax reform package within an acceptable time frame. (INQUIRER/BUSINESS DAILY/MALAYA)

- The Board of Investments is pushing for a five-year extension of the three percent duty on imported capital equipment, which will expire at year-end, in lieu of the non-passage of other fiscal incentives. (BULLETIN)

- The National Power Corp is expected to suffer losses of six billion pesos this year when its big industrial clients start looking for new sources of electricity other than the state-owned utility. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
